title: Warren Buffett at UNC 1996: character, circle of confidence, moats and why he ignores the market
summary: Buffett fields student questions on hiring and character, staying inside a circle of confidence, buying great businesses and rarely selling, moats and franchise value, ignoring market forecasts, his shareholder base, and mistakes of omission.

principles.text: Character traits are habits you can choose; form the good ones early, because habits harden.
principles.quote: the chains of habit are too like to be felt until they're too heavy to be broken

principles.text: Stay in your circle of confidence; knowing where its edges are matters more than its size.
principles.quote: the most important thing in terms of your circle of confidence is not how large the area of it is it's how well you've defined the perimeter

principles.text: Ignore market and rate forecasts; buy the right business at the right price with the right people.
principles.quote: all i know is if i buy the right kind of business the right price with the right people i'll do well over time

principles.text: A franchise is a moat around an economic castle; judge both castle size and moat durability.
principles.quote: franchise is basically like a moat around your economic castle now there's two things are important how big is the castle

principles.text: Selling a truly great business because the price looks high is almost always a mistake.
principles.quote: to sell off something that is a really wonderful business because the price looks a little high or something like that it's almost always a mistake

principles.text: Distrust accounting footnotes you can't understand; if you can't understand it, don't invest.
principles.quote: if it's written so you can't understand it i am very suspicious
